evidence.text: Stryker said on its Q2-2026 call (2026-07-31) that a supply disruption at one Inari plant created a significant backorder and lost peripheral-vascular sales (US vascular organic -6.7%), with backorders expected back to a manageable level only by the END of calendar Q3 - i.e. the market leader's VTE clot-removal line (FlowTriever/ClotTriever) was supply-constrained across ANGO's entire fiscal Q1 (June-August 2026), a window in which AngioVac/AlphaVac (MT, $11.1m in FQ4, ~14% of sales) could pick up cases; consensus and the EW preview frame MT as a stalled franchise after FQ4's -1.1%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MT was the growth story through FY26 (+41% in Q1 FY26, +17.9% in Q3); the Q3 FY26 print with MT +17.9% still fell -13.7% (Apr 2026), and FQ4 with MT -1.1% rose +1.7% on the guide, so this line has not visibly driven the reaction on its own.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Inari backorder is in a large-cap's call and is not in any ANGO preview read (EW 2026-09-30 discusses only ANGO's own sales-force reset and competition as headwinds). If priced, the preview narrative would be MT share recapture and the stock would not have slid 6.9% into the print. Caveat sized in: Penumbra (US revenue +17.1% in Apr-Jun) is the more obvious beneficiary, and the disruption already overlapped part of ANGO's FQ4 (Mar-May) in which MT still declined, so the share pickup may be small; net of the rest of the company MT is only ~14% of sales.
evidence.independence: Proxy (counterparty statement, not confirmed by ANGO). evidence.text: Mechanical thrombectomy faces its toughest comp of the year in FQ1: Q1 FY26 MT was $11.3m, +41.2% (8-K 2025-10-02), while the run-rate had fallen to $11.1m and -1.1% in FQ4 with AngioVac -15.8%, prompting a commercial reorganization ('changed our commercial approach... new leadership structure'); flat sequential MT would print roughly -2% YoY, a second straight decline, against a VTE market where Penumbra grew US revenue 17%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 (Jul-2026) MT -1.1% was masked by a total beat and above-consensus FY27 guide; stock +1.7%. No print yet where MT decline was the headline.

If fully priced, the preview would not need to frame the sales-force reset as an open question. evidence.text: The two expansion leases management called 'advanced' on 2026-07-27 are still undisclosed. On that call it said it was in talks with two existing customers for about 100 MW and 150 MW of expansion, at 'materially higher rates than their current leases', and that it was marketing a further 1.7 GW. EDGAR shows no 8-K from APLD between 2026-07-27 and 2026-10-07 (only Forms 4, ARS, DEF 14A and POSASR), so neither lease had been signed and disclosed as of early October. This print is where the stock has historically moved on lease news: +31% (Jul-2025, CoreWeave), +16% (Oct-2025, PF2 talks), +8% (Jan-2026, 900 MW pipeline). When there was no new pipeline news it moved -8% and +0.9%. A signed expansion at higher rates would also answer the bear case that the 810 MW of hyperscaler leases were priced below peers.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lease and pipeline news packaged with the print: +31.01% (2025-07-30), +16.05% (2025-10-09), +8.05% (2026-01-07). Prints without new lease news: -7.99% (2026-04-08) and +0.93% (2026-07-27; the Delta Forge 2 lease had been announced on June 8 before that print).
evidence.why_not_priced: Had the market expected these leases, the stock would not be 52% off its high, it would not have fallen 6% on a $70 Buy initiation, and the skew would not lean to downside. Talks first disclosed 10 weeks ago with no filing since read as stale. The two-sided risk is real: if management says on the call that the expansions slipped, the yield bear case gets stronger. The Finland site released the day before the print had no tenant (https://ir.applieddigital.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/162/applied-digital-secures-up-to-1-gw-of-potential-power), which is weak evidence that no lease was ready to headline.
evidence.independence: The EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001144879&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) independently confirms that no lease 8-K has been filed since 2026-07-27. The same 100/150 MW claim also appears in trefis's 2026-09-03 article (same call, so the same source). Needham's estimate raise for 150 MW of Delta Forge expansion was cited in a webull summary, date unverified.

evidence.text: FQ1 revenue probably clears the $115-135m bar. Base rent alone should rise from $44.1m to about $65-70m: Building 1 at 100 MW for the full quarter plus Building 2 Phase 1 (75 MW, ready for service 2026-06-30) for July-August. Add about $37m of data-center hosting and about $18m of cloud. That totals about $125-135m GAAP before any tenant fit-out revenue. Fit-out revenue is lumpy and tied to deliveries: $18.9m in FQ3 and $152.4m in FQ4, booked ahead of the 2026-06-30 handover. Building 2 Phase 2 was handed over on 2026-10-02 and the Polaris Forge 2 buildings are entering fit-out, so another fit-out tranche in FQ1 is plausible. Consensus of $115-135m appears to model none.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ4 revenue of $258.7m against a consensus of about $95-104m (2.5x) bought +0.93% (2026-07-27). FQ3 revenue of $126.6m, a beat, was sold -7.99% (2026-04-08) on a wider GAAP loss. On the last two prints the name has not paid for revenue beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: If consensus included fit-out revenue it would sit near or above FQ4's $258.7m rather than $115-135m. The market appears to treat fit-out as pass-through, at roughly 15% gross margin, which is why this finding is small.
evidence.independence: FQ3 fit-out of $18.9m is in the FQ3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1144879/000114487926000029/apldq326earningsrelease.htm). The 10-K says FY26 fit-out totalled $270.6m at PF1 and that heavy construction continues through FY27 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001144879/000114487926000048/apld-20260531.htm).
